svg.title: Diode envelope detector circuit and choosing its RC time constant
svg.desc: A diode envelope detector: an AM signal source feeds a diode, whose output charges a capacitor C with a resistor R in parallel to ground; the voltage across them is the envelope output. The rule for the time constant is 1 over the carrier frequency much less than RC much less than 1 over the message bandwidth W. Below, three simulated outputs for the same AM input: RC too short follows each carrier cycle down and leaves a large sawtooth ripple; RC about right follows the envelope with a small ripple; RC too long cannot fall fast enough and cuts across the troughs of the envelope (diagonal clipping). Worked example for AM radio: carrier 1 MHz, audio up to 5 kHz, 80% modulation: R = 10 kilohms and C = 2.2 nanofarads give RC = 22 microseconds, between 1 microsecond and the 24 microsecond limit for 80% modulation.
svg.text: Simulated output (orange) for one AM input (blue), with the true envelope dashed
